report.numbers: Expert beats Random 99.9%, Greedy 90.4%, Racer 82.6% (400 games each, seats alternated, draws count half); Expert plan equals Greedy plan in 47.2% of 6,024 decisions; seat A wins 50.4% of 400 Expert mirror games; 0 games hit the round cap; Expert passes all three set positions on 5 seeds each. Draws: 35% of Expert mirror games, 47% of Racer mirror games end with both players at 0 in the same round. Games last 6.5 rounds (Expert mirror).
loop: Each round a player picks the cards that fill the mana (Expert leaves mana unspent in 27% of rounds, 0.38 a round), aims its Hits, and sends each unit at the player or at a unit.

Hits land before attacks, so the real choice is which enemy unit to remove before it swings; Expert aims most Hits at units and sends 90% of attacks at the player, because an attack at the player takes nothing back while an attack at a unit takes its attack back (twice if both attack each other).

Best play boils down to: race, spend Hits on the attacker that out-races you, trade with a unit only when it kills something big for free. Predicting the other plan is mostly guessing which of your units their Hits will remove, not where their units will attack.
The simultaneous last round makes mutual kills common: a third of Expert mirror games are draws.
report.cost: Mana binds every round: a card in hand is priced out in 98.9% of rounds and the hand is never emptied (1%). Mana never reaches its cap of 10, because games end by round 6-7.
